events.title: Public Good Investment Option replaces Alternative Investment Option; real estate limited to approved developments
events.description: From January 2023 the Alternative Investment Option is replaced by the Public Good Investment Option (minimum US$175,000); only Approved Developments qualify for the real estate route; existing Approved Private Homes and AIO developments must reapply within 45 days of the new regulations.
events.quote: From January 2023 onwards, the Alternative Investment Option (AIO) under the current CBI Programme is to be replaced by the newly introduced Public Good Investment Option (PGIO)

events.title: US$10 million affordable housing project announced under the Public Benefit Option
events.description: The CIU Chairman lists among 2025 milestones the announcement of a US$10 million Affordable Housing Project under the Public Benefit Option with ring-fenced funds, the launch of the Saturn digital application platform, signing of the Eastern Caribbean CBI Regulatory Framework, and a first cohort of a Micro and Small Business Grant Programme (EC$360,000 to 36 entrepreneurs; funding source not stated).
events.quote: Announcement of a US$10 million Affordable Housing Project under the Public Benefit Option, supported by rigorous financial reporting and ring-fenced funds.

events.title: Transition fees for applications under previous options
events.description: The CSI Regulations 2023 require applications made under the previous Alternative Investment Option and Real Estate Option (CBI Regulations 2011) to pay post-approval-in-principle application fees within 90 days of approval in principle (e.g. US$50,000 per main applicant for the previous real estate option).
events.quote: The following updates regarding previous investment options were introduced in the Saint Christopher and Nevis Citizenship by Substantial Investment Regulations 2023 (the CSI Regulations 2023) on 27 July 2023 and have come into effect.

events.title: Iranian nationals suspended from the CBI programme
events.description: According to FinCEN, the St Kitts and Nevis government announced in 2013 that all Iranian nationals were suspended from the programme; FinCEN believed Iranian nationals continued to obtain passports through it.
events.quote: in 2013 the SKN government announced that all Iranian nationals were suspended from participating in the SKN Citizenship-by-Investment program.

events.title: Limited time offer extended to January 2024 (then overridden)
events.description: IMF Box (from press reports): in June 2023 the CIU CEO announced the SGF limited time offer would be extended by seven months to 31 January 2024 because of 'overwhelming demand'; the July 2023 price doubling overrode the extension with immediate effect.
events.location: PDF p. 66 (printed p. 62), Annex IX Box 1
events.quote: June 2023. CIU CEO announced that the LTO would be extended by seven months until 1/31/24 due to “an overwhelming demand”.

events.title: CIU head resigns; technical committee restructured
events.description: IMF Box (from press reports): the CIU CEO resigned in September 2024 and the oversight mechanism was restructured, the technical committee to include the Permanent Secretary for National Security, two civil servants appointed by the Minister, the CIU CEO and a Board of Governors representative.
events.location: PDF p. 66 (printed p. 62), Annex IX Box 1
events.quote: The CBI oversight mechanism was restructured, so that the technical committee would include the PS for National Security, two civil servants appointed by the Minister, the CIU CEO, and a BoG representative.

events.title: Tonga Trust Fund set up, funded by passport sales
events.description: IMF working paper Table 5 and Appendix Table A1: the Tonga Trust Fund (inception 1988), with stabilization and development objectives, was funded by the sale of Tongan passports to foreigners and the lease of satellite space; withdrawal rules unknown; its portfolio was invested entirely in three US companies and suffered large losses.
events.location: PDF p. 27 (printed p. 26), Table 5; PDF p. 34 (printed p. 33), Table A1
events.quote: Sale of Tongan passports to foreigners; revenue from lease of Tongan satellite space

events.title: Belize economic citizenship programme operating (1995-2002 per IMF)

new_indicators.definition: cbi_programme_costs (e.g. CBI due diligence costs in the fiscal accounts) divided by GDP, as stated by the source.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-kna1 for IMF St Kitts Article IV tables (General Government Fiscal Operations in percent of GDP, row "of which: CBI due diligence costs").

new_indicators.name: Primary fiscal balance excluding CBI proceeds
new_indicators.definition: General government primary balance (before interest) excluding CBI receipts (and related items the source names, e.g. development-fund grants, investment proceeds, due diligence costs), as a share of GDP.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-kna1 for IMF St Kitts Article IV Table 3b. Companion to fiscal_balance_excl_cbi_pct_gdp (overall balance).

new_indicators.name: Current account balance excluding CBI receipts
new_indicators.definition: External current account balance excluding CBI receipts recorded in it (e.g. CBI budgetary fees booked as services exports), as a share of GDP, as stated by the source.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-kna1 for IMF St Kitts Article IV balance of payments tables.

new_indicators.name: CBI dividend paid to citizens, share of GDP
new_indicators.definition: cbi_dividend_payout divided by GDP, as stated by the source.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-kna1 for IMF St Kitts 2025 Article IV Table 2 (row "CBI dividend").

new_indicators.name: CBI development-fund spending as a share of GDP
new_indicators.definition: Spending of a national development fund financed by CBI contributions (e.g. St Kitts SIDF) in a period, divided by GDP, as stated by the source. Use breakdown category= for components (transfers to government, grants, direct programmes, net-of-budget presentations).
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-kna1 for IMF WP/15/93 Box 5 (SIDF operations 2007-2013). Companion to ndf_income_pct_gdp.

new_indicators.name: CBI development-fund surplus as a share of GDP
new_indicators.definition: Income minus spending of a national development fund financed by CBI contributions in a period, divided by GDP, as stated by the source.
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-kna1 for IMF WP/15/93 Box 5 (SIDF surplus 2007-2013).

new_indicators.name: CBI money as a share of government expenditure
new_indicators.definition: CBI money received by the government in a period divided by total government expenditure in that period, as calculated by the source (how much of spending CBI receipts paid for).
new_indicators.notes: Proposed by extract-cbi-kna1 for the St Kitts 2023 Budget Address ('funded 63.5 percent of the Government's Total Expenditure' in 2021). Different denominator from cbi_fiscal_revenue_pct_revenue.
